title: What YOU need to do before the Forum Shuts Down!

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Hi everyone.
The RMW Refugee Discord has been working very hard to archive everything here and build our new home. We understand that not everyone wants to join the Discord or may not have Discord to begin with, and that's okay! You're not getting singled out, so we want to share some points with you.
THIS IS IMPORTANT IF YOU INTEND TO TRANSITION TO THE NEW HOME!
Here are the bullet points.
What you need to do right away:
Make back ups of private messages
Make back ups of your bookmarks
Post info you are comfortable sharing publicly here
(we'll use this info to cross-reference/get in contact with you to verify it's you signing up to the new site, not an impersonator. Maybe we can also use it to carry over some forum stats.)
Change your signature to include the temporary domain:
https://rpg-refuge.com/
(check my signature for an example)
mention rpg-refuge.com or the RMW Refugee Discord (
https://discord.gg/NNT2JdgQa
) any time you can on RMW (while avoiding being an obnoxious spammer)
Know what's going on:
RPG Refugee Discord is 600+ (and growing) members.
Manual and automatic archival efforts are going on.
There are 3 known projects from different groups using bot crawlers to scrape the entire website
Numerous individuals are manually backing up pages to archive.org's Way Back Machine
All the mods and some admins are in the Discord helping discuss archival & migrating to a new site.
There are lots of discussions about setting up the new site
We will avoid using Discourse, the (imo, ugly) software RPG Maker Guild uses.
We are having lengthy discussions about...
How to support the forum for decades to come, even when user population is low
How to encourage user growth, rather than stagnation and reliance on GGG products
What features are important or should be added to make it a useful home for members and randos hunting Google for support info.
Maybe attaching a wiki to the new site?
What you can do (now and after the forum shuts down)
You can join the RMW Refugee Discord:
https://discord.gg/NNT2JdgQa
Stay up to date with the discussions involving archival and migration
You can help with the archival and migration process!
Even if you can't, lively chatter keeps people excited and motivated, so come chat - it's actually an important role!
Spread the word about RMW Refugee Discord, more people = more help.
Spread the word about rpg-refuge.com
(You can spread the word about both the discord and website anywhere, including your favorite social media sites!)
Join rpgmaker.net - the folks there are kind and welcoming everyone departing RMW.
I encourage you to really consider your next GGG product purchase or use of their services...
(my personal opinion is that you should not join RPG Maker Guild...please join rpgmaker.net instead)
Right now, you can access and freely browse this archive:
RPG Maker Forum Archive — 14 Years of Community, Preserved
Threads, tutorials, and plugins from the RPG Maker Web forum — saved and searchable before it closes Dec 11, 2026.
rpgmakerchat.com
It is still scraping the website, so at the time of writing it is incomplete at 9%. Likely within a couple months the full website will be fully scraped.

The crawlers will persist after the forum goes read-only.
In fact, Archive Team -- a team dedicated to archiving the web -- has agreed to assist in archiving RMW, but they stated they won't begin the archival process until after the forum goes read-only.
So, rest assured, even topics made since the closure announcement will be archived too.

posts.author: whtdragon
posts.body:
ZENWARECO said:
How do I backup?
Click to expand...
unfortunately, the easiest way to back up (that doesn't involve scraper software or bots) is either through copy/pasting text manually, or right clicking and "save page as" and saving the whole webpage you're looking at in a folder on your computer and/or device. This information can later be sorted out by either you or someone else.

posts.author: Mac15001900
posts.body: And for bookmarks, just open all of them and then add them as browser bookmarks. You'll then have half a year to sort through those.
